svg.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Investment Process
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-first-thirty-days; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Documented Investment Process; subtitle: Build the operating system before expecting investment proceeds.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four consecutive work periods cover Days 1–30. Numeric values are each period's ending day, not revenue or deal counts. The canonical first-deal window remains 3–10 months; the sprint produces diligence and operating artifacts rather than promising an acquisition, redemption, or foreclosure.; caption: A completed sprint leaves a traceable county rulebook, tested parcel records, conservative bid worksheets, and a funded cash plan. An unsuitable auction remains a valid reason to finish the month without deploying acquisition capital.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one jurisdiction and document its rules; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select one county and asset type. Archive its official auction packet, registration instructions, payment requirements, redemption statute, and enforcement procedure. Ask local counsel to identify notice, bankruptcy, federal lien, and surplus issues.; label: Days 8-14; value: Build and test the parcel evidence register; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Create a SQLite register keyed by county and parcel identifier. Import one published sale file, retain source dates, and manually audit twenty records against assessor GIS, recorder documents, and counsel's title-review requirements.; label: Days 15-21; value: Model bids, reserves, and delayed cash recovery; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Create spreadsheet bid worksheets separating principal, premiums, interest-bearing amounts, fees, and taxes. Stress redemption at 6, 18, and 36 months where legally relevant, plus capital loss; test reserve adequacy without assuming immediate owner distributions.; label: Days 22-30; value: Rehearse execution and verify cash classifications; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Run a mock auction against documented bid ceilings, test redemption alerts, and reconcile sample receipts into principal and earnings. Confirm contractor scope, payment procedures, and record retention; fund a real purchase only when its specific checks pass.

text.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Investment Process
text.tspan: Thirty Days to a Documented Investment Process

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one jurisdiction and document its rules; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select one county and asset type. Archive its official auction packet, registration instructions, payment requirements, redemption statute, and enforcement procedure. Ask local counsel to identify notice, bankruptcy, federal lien, and surplus issues.

text.title: Choose one jurisdiction and document its rules

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Build and test the parcel evidence register; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Create a SQLite register keyed by county and parcel identifier. Import one published sale file, retain source dates, and manually audit twenty records against assessor GIS, recorder documents, and counsel's title-review requirements.

text.title: Build and test the parcel evidence register

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Model bids, reserves, and delayed cash recovery; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Create spreadsheet bid worksheets separating principal, premiums, interest-bearing amounts, fees, and taxes. Stress redemption at 6, 18, and 36 months where legally relevant, plus capital loss; test reserve adequacy without assuming immediate owner distributions.

text.title: Model bids, reserves, and delayed cash recovery

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Rehearse execution and verify cash classifications; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Run a mock auction against documented bid ceilings, test redemption alerts, and reconcile sample receipts into principal and earnings. Confirm contractor scope, payment procedures, and record retention; fund a real purchase only when its specific checks pass.

text.title: Rehearse execution and verify cash classifications

Assumptions: Four consecutive work periods cover Days 1–30. Numeric values are each period's ending day, not revenue or deal counts. The canonical first-deal window remains 3–10 months; the sprint produces diligence and operating artifacts rather than promising an acquisition, redemption, or foreclosure.
